model.name: Token Loader
model.description:
Generate a `tokens.json` using something like Style Dictionary.


example tokens.json:


[
{
"name": "core/color/black",
"value": "#000000"
},
{
"name": "alias/color/black",
"value": "#000000",
"aliasOf": "core/color/black"
}

Typescript types for the tokens:


interface VariableToken {
name: string; // an/example/name
value: unknown;
}

interface AliasToken extends VariableToken {

model.description:
Synapse helps design system teams understand, audit, and maintain complex Figma variable architectures.


It turns local variables, styles, aliases, modes, and component usage into an interactive dependency graph. This makes it easier to trace relationships, identify unused or broken tokens, review downstream impact, and safely restructure large systems.


Built For

Design system designers and architects working with large token libraries, multiple modes, and deeply connected components.


NEW: Variable Reassignment Wizard

Repair a whole library in minutes. Swapped your entire token system? Reassignment re-binds every component, style, and mode to the new variables in one safe, resumable run. Auto-detects what needs fixing, matches by path and value, and surfaces orphaned modes and unmapped bindings so you know exactly what still needs work.


What It Does

  1. Visualizes variables, styles, aliases, and token tiers (Supports up to 3 Tiers)
  2. Traces dependencies and component usage
  3. Highlights unused, unresolved, and circular references
  4. Supports Light, Dark, and additional modes
  5. Imports and exports common design-token formats
  6. Reassigns legacy variable and style bindings during migrations
  7. Provides focused editing, rewiring, diagnostics, and impact analysis
  8. Uses asynchronous scanning and caching for large Figma files


What It Does Not Do

Synapse does not automatically decide how your design system should be structured. Ambiguous mappings remain visible for review instead of being guessed.

Some large migrations require preparation, confirmation, and a final review in Figma. Changes are applied through Figma’s Plugin API and are not a replacement for versioning or backups.


Privacy And Maintenance

No account is required. Synapse does not connect to external services or upload your design-system data.


The plugin is actively maintained because we use it ourselves in production design-system work. Improvements are driven by real libraries, real migrations, and real everyday problems.

model.description:
Introduction

Clean up your Figma files with one click. Identify and remove unused components, empty groups, hidden layers, and redundant structures to improve organization and performance.


Function Description

•Automatically scans the file and visualizes issues

•Supports batch removal of unused components, styles, and variables

•Suggests optimizations by risk level: safe, medium, and high

•Allows selecting and highlighting specific items for review

•Supports multilingual UI (EN, ZH, JA, KO, HI, etc.)


How to Use

1.Click “Scan” to analyze the current file

2.Review categorized results and select items to clean

3.Use “Optimize Selected” for batch optimization

4.Click individual items to highlight them in Figma


Notes

•High-risk suggestions are informational only—handle with care

•Optimization actions are not reversible; save your version beforehand

•Shared components in libraries will not be deleted


介绍

一键清理 Figma 设计文件，智能识别未使用组件、空组、隐藏图层、冗余结构等，提高设计整洁度与加载性能。


功能说明

•自动扫描设计文件，输出可视化优化建议

•支持批量清理未使用组件、变量、样式

•分级优化建议：安全项、中等风险、高风险

•支持查看并选中问题图层，逐项优化

•多语言支持（中/英/日/韩/印地语等）


使用方法

1.打开插件后点击「Scan」扫描当前文件

2.查看分类结果并选择需要优化的子项

3.点击「Optimize Selected」进行一键清理

4.可逐项点击查看详情并定位图层


注意事项

•高风险项仅提示建议，需谨慎处理

•优化操作不可撤销，建议先保存版本

•插件不会自动删除组件库中共享资源

model.name: Variable Audit
model.description:
Design systems make it easy to answer "where is this variable used?" The harder question is the opposite one: where should a variable have been used, and wasn't? That is the hardcoded #0D99FF on a button, the magic 24px gap, the raw corner radius someone typed in a hurry.


Variable Audit scans your file and answers three questions.



COVERAGE: what is missing

A single adoption score, broken down by category (color, spacing, radius, stroke, typography), by page, and by top-level frame, so you can say "Checkout is at 34%" instead of guessing.


The score separates variables from styles, because a file can score well on color and text styles while using no variables at all. If nothing is bound to a variable, the plugin says so plainly rather than letting styles flatter the number.


Every hardcoded value is listed and ranked by how often it appears, each matched to the variable it should have been. Matches respect variable scopes, so a corner radius token is never suggested for a fill, and every suggestion carries a confidence level. Click any finding to jump straight to the layer.



USAGE: where your variables actually are

A complete map of every binding: which variable, which property, which page, frame and layer. Search it, expand any variable to see its layers, click a row to select that layer on canvas, or select every layer using a variable at once. Run this before renaming or changing a token, so you know what you are about to affect.



CLEANUP: what is actually safe to remove

Local variables that nothing in the file reaches.


Unlike a naive scan, this follows alias chains, so a primitive referenced only by a semantic token is never reported as deletable. Hidden layers are always searched for usage, which means hiding a layer never makes its token look unused.



SCAN WHAT YOU NEED

Scope a run to the whole file, the current page, or just your selection.

Selection and page scans return in seconds, so you can check a frame while you work. A 500,000 layer design system takes a few minutes for a full pass, stays responsive throughout, and any scan can be cancelled part way.



EXPORTS

Everything downloads as CSV: coverage by page and frame, untokenized values with their suggested tokens, per layer detail, the full usage map, and cleanup candidates.



DETAILS

Light, dark and automatic themes, with your choice remembered between runs.


No network access at all. The manifest forbids it, so nothing leaves your machine and nothing is collected. The plugin never writes to your file: suggestions are reported, not applied.



ONE HONEST LIMITATION

Figma gives plugins no way to see whether other files use a variable, so anything published to a library is flagged in the cleanup list. Treat that list as "investigate these", not "delete these".

model.name: Design System Auditor
model.description:
Design System Auditor scans your Figma file and tells you exactly how consistent it is with your design system — then gives you a single Health Score to track over time.


Stop eyeballing files for stray hex codes and off-scale spacing. Run a scan and get a prioritized list of every inconsistency, why it matters, and — where it's safe to do so — a one-click fix.


How it works


Pick a scope (your current selection, the active page, or the whole file), hit Scan, and the plugin walks every layer locally inside Figma — no upload, no server, no account.


What it checks


🎨 Colors — hard-coded fills/strokes, near-duplicate colors, colors that should be using a style or variable, unused Paint Styles


🔤 Typography — inconsistent font sizes/families/weights, text not linked to a text style, an exploding number of one-off type combinations


📐 Spacing — Auto Layout gaps and padding that don't match your spacing scale


🏷️ Naming — "Frame 128," "Rectangle 12," and friends; duplicate sibling names; components that break your naming convention


🧩 Components (Pro) — duplicated component patterns that should be one component set, ungrouped variants, bloated variant counts, possible detached instances


🔗 Variables (Pro) — hard-coded values that match an existing variable, unused variables, near-duplicate variables, inconsistent naming


♿ Accessibility (Pro) — WCAG contrast ratios, undersized text, small touch targets — clearly labeled Pass/Warning/Fail with an honest note on what's automated vs. what needs a human look


Your Health Score


One number, 0–100, broken down by category — Excellent, Good, Needs Attention, or Critical — so you can watch it improve (or catch regressions) scan over scan.


Fully configurable


Set your own color swatches, type scale, spacing scale, and naming convention in Settings. The audit checks against your design system, not a generic default.


Safe by design


Nothing is ever changed automatically. Every fix is deterministic (like rounding 17px to your nearest scale value of 16px) and requires an explicit confirmation before anything touches your file. Undo works exactly like it always does — Cmd/Ctrl+Z.


Privacy first


Your design data never leaves Figma. No network requests, no analytics, no third-party AI. The only thing stored is your own design-system settings, saved locally via Figma's own storage.
model.tagline: Know your design system's health score in one scan.

model.name: DS Tuner Live
model.description:
DS Tuner Live brings WYSIWYG token tuning to Figma. Drag a slider and watch every component, text style, and frame using your Design System Variables update across the entire file — in real time.


Three tabs, one workflow:

• Semantic — designer-friendly sliders (Display Title, Paragraph Content, Card Roundness, H/V Page Margin, Between Sections…). Font-size sliders auto-couple line-height so text never collapses when you scale.

• Token — raw variable access grouped by Type / Spacing / Radius. Slider ranges auto-infer per type (letter-spacing precision step 0.05, line-height 10–140, etc.).

• Retrofit — select any frame and one-click bind all hardcoded padding, gap, corner radius, font size, line height, letter spacing values to nearest DS variables. Also intelligently applies DS text styles when matched.


Built for real Design Systems:

• Mode-aware — Desktop / Mobile modes detected automatically. Editing one mode never touches the other.

• Selection highlight — click any node, the plugin highlights every variable it depends on.

• Usage tracking — variables not used anywhere are dimmed and labeled "unused" so you know which sliders actually affect your file.

• Color variables intentionally skipped — color DS is frozen by brand guideline.


Naming convention (auto-mapped):

font/size/h1 · font/lineHeight/h1 · font/letterSpacing/h1 · font/family/english

spacing/md_button-padding · radius/lg_card · layout/page-edge-h

Add semantic _[use-case] suffixes to make tokens self-documenting.


Brand-agnostic — works on any Figma DS file that follows the conventions above. Color variables are intentionally skipped (color DS is frozen by brand guidelines).


Perfect for design system maintainers, design leads on multi-mode (desktop/mobile) projects, and anyone retrofitting an existing file with DS Variables.

model.name: IconAutomation
model.description:
### **Comprehensive Guide to the IconAutomation Figma Plugin**


#### **Introduction**


**IconAutomation** is a powerful tool designed to streamline and automate the process of publishing icons within Figma. By integrating with GitLab CI, this plugin ensures your icon sets are always up-to-date and consistent across all platforms. Whether you're a designer working on a small project or part of a large team managing complex design systems, IconAutomation saves time and effort while eliminating manual workflows.


This plugin is primarily tailored for enterprise scenarios. Our company aims to build an internal icon library using Figma and GitLab as a replacement for Iconfont, which suffers from the following limitations:


- **Management Complexity**: Managing Iconfont requires multiple accounts and frequent importing/exporting between design files, Iconfont platforms, and code repositories.

- **Icon Accumulation**: Over time, unused icons accumulate and are loaded all at once in projects, preventing on-demand loading.

- **Font-Based Limitations**: Font-based icons may render blurry or pixelated on high-resolution screens.

- **Icon Conflicts**: Conflicts can arise when using multiple Iconfont libraries, leading to incorrect icon displays.


IconAutomation addresses these issues by leveraging SVGs to build a scalable internal icon library. Once configured, updating both the icon library and code repository can be done with a single click. Unlike font-based solutions, SVGs enable granular control over icon usage—only the icons actually used in a project are bundled, preventing unnecessary bloat.


#### **Core Features**


- **One-Click Publishing**: Publish icons directly from Figma with a single action.

- **GitLab Integration**: Seamlessly connect with GitLab CI/CD pipelines for automated workflows.

- **Version Control**: Automatically manage semantic versioning in `package.json`.

- **Diff Generation**: Compare current and historical icons to generate detailed change reports.

- **Branch Automation**: Create feature branches, submit merge requests (MRs), and clean up temporary branches automatically.

- **SVG Optimization**: Optimize icon assets for performance using industry-standard tools.


#### **Prerequisites**


- **GitLab Instance**: A deployed GitLab instance (cloud-based or self-hosted).

- **Template Repository**: Deploy the `react-icons` template repository to your GitLab instance.

- **Figma Client**: Install the IconAutomation plugin via Figma's Community portal.

- **Plugin Configuration**: Configure essential settings as outlined below.


#### **Configuration Guide**


##### **GitLab Settings**


- **Domain**: The URL of your GitLab instance (e.g., `https://gitlab.com`).

- **Project ID**: Found under your repository’s **Settings > General**.

- **Access Token**: Generate a token with `api`, `read_repository`, and `write_repository` scopes from GitLab’s **Profile > Access Tokens**.


##### **Figma Plugin Setup**


1. Install the plugin and grant necessary permissions.

2. Navigate to the plugin settings and input your GitLab domain, project ID, and access token.

3. Validate the connection to ensure seamless integration.


#### **Design Specifications**


##### **Page Naming Conventions**


- Pages intended for publishing **must** include the keyword "icon" (e.g., `product-icons`, `system-icons`).

- Only frames under these pages will be processed by the plugin.


##### **Frame Requirements**


- Frames must be named with one of the following suffixes:

- **Outlined**: For icons with stroke-based designs (e.g., `Navigation-Outlined`).

- **Filled**: For solid-filled icons (e.g., `Actions-Filled`).

- **Colored**: For multi-color icons, further categorized as:

- **Light**: Optimized for light backgrounds.

- **Dark**: Optimized for dark backgrounds.


##### **Icon Layer Rules**


- All icons **must** be Figma components (not frames or groups).

- Verify component status by selecting a layer—the top panel should display "Component."


##### **Naming Standards**


- Use **Upper Camel Case** (e.g., `AlertCircle`, `SettingsGear`).

- Append style suffixes (e.g., `AlertCircleOutlined`, `SettingsGearFilled`).

- Avoid special characters (`-`, `_`, spaces) and numeric suffixes unless intrinsic to the icon’s name (e.g., `Star1` is allowed; `Star 1` is invalid).

- Ensure uniqueness within each category to prevent conflicts.


#### **Automated Workflow**


1. **Repository Setup**: Configure GitLab details in the plugin settings.

2. **Local Validation**:

- The plugin checks for naming compliance, duplicates, and structural errors.

- Invalid icons are flagged with actionable feedback.

3. **Branch Management**:

- A temporary branch (e.g., `figma-update-20231001`) is created from `master`.

- Semantic versioning updates `package.json` (e.g., `1.2.0` → `1.3.0` for minor changes).

4. **Diff Analysis**:

- Compares current icons against the latest `master` commit.

- Generates a report detailing additions, modifications, and deletions.

5. **Asset Export**:

- Exports SVGs via Figma’s API and organizes them into folders (e.g., `/outlined`, `/filled`).

- Applies SVGO optimizations to reduce file size.

6. **Merge Request (MR)**:

- Submits an MR with a standardized title (e.g., `[Figma]: add icons`).

- Auto-merges after passing CI checks (linting, build tests).


#### **Best Practices**


- **Consistent Naming**: Adhere strictly to naming conventions to avoid validation failures.

- **Modular Design**: Build icons as reusable components with standardized dimensions (e.g., 24x24px).

- **Version Tracking**: Maintain a `CHANGELOG.md` to document icon updates and deprecations.

- **Performance Checks**: Audit SVG complexity to ensure optimal rendering (e.g., simplify paths for small icons).


#### **Example Scenarios**


##### **Scenario 1: Updating an Icon Set**


1. Add new icons to the `Actions-Filled` frame in Figma.

2. Run the plugin to validate and generate diffs.

3. Submit an MR to deploy changes to production.


##### **Scenario 2: Migrating Legacy Iconfont Icons**


1. Import existing Iconfont SVGs into a `Legacy-Outlined` frame.

2. Use the plugin to publish them as SVGs and update project imports.


#### **Troubleshooting**


| Issue | Solution |

| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |

| **Naming Errors** | Check for invalid characters or duplicates using the plugin’s validation tool. |

| **Merge Conflicts** | Resolve conflicts manually in GitLab before re-running the plugin. |

| **API Timeouts** | Increase timeout thresholds in GitLab CI settings or split large icon sets. |

| **SVG Rendering Issues** | Convert strokes to outlines and simplify complex paths in Figma. |


#### **Future Roadmap**


- [ ] **GitHub Integration**: Support publishing to GitHub repositories.

- [ ] **Change Preview**: Display a summary of icon changes before publishing.

- [ ] **Enhanced Error Handling**: Provide contextual error messages with resolution steps.

- [ ] **Progress Tracking**: Add a visual progress bar for long-running tasks.


#### **Additional Resources**


- **Figma Documentation**: [Figma Help Center](https://help.figma.com)

- **GitLab CI/CD Guide**: [GitLab CI/CD Documentation](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/)

- **Community Support**: Join discussions on Figma’s [Community Forum](https://forum.figma.com).
